profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility, internally identified in public records as Albany 4, is located at 10 Airline Drive, Colonie, NY 12205, in the Albany metro area; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

New York State has moved to slow data center growth even as Albany-area proposals advance. Governor Hochul announced a one-year statewide moratorium, effective July 8, 2026, on state environmental permits for data centers of 50 megawatts or more, pending new regulatory frameworks on energy demand, water use, air quality, and ratepayer impact; NYISO recorded 51 large data-load project requests statewide in 2026, up from just 6 in 2022. In Albany itself, developer Guild Ventures has proposed a multibillion-dollar mixed-use tech campus at the 76-acre Kenwood Commons site in the city's South End, with a data center component that could draw up to 100 megawatts; Albany's Common Council was separately weighing local zoning rules, since the city currently has no data-center-specific zoning category.

reading.body:
Lumen Albany 4 is a carrier-neutral colocation facility in Colonie, New York, part of Lumen's network of 175-plus edge data centers across North America. Lumen does not publish capacity figures for any individual site, and the operator's product design targets cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range per tenant rather than wholesale hyperscale deployment. Without published specifications, the campus cannot be assessed for AI infrastructure density or workload suitability.

New York State imposed a one-year moratorium on state environmental permits for data centers of 50 megawatts or more, effective July 8, 2026, creating regulatory uncertainty for large deployments statewide even as demand signals remain strong: NYISO recorded 51 large data-load project requests in 2026, up from 6 in 2022. Albany itself has no data-center-specific zoning category, and the city is separately evaluating local rules while a private developer proposes a 100-megawatt data center campus at a separate site.

This facility ranks second among New York's mapped data centers by published capacity, though only one facility statewide has disclosed megawatt figures to this registry. The absence of published specifications for Lumen's site reflects an operator-wide policy gap, not missing research, and leaves its role in New York's AI infrastructure contribution unmeasurable from public sources.
